<root>: usage: book_splitter [-h] {convert,tools,inspect,split,scan,preprocess,dictionary,chunk,chunk-glossary,matter,translate,concatenate,assemble,postprocess,openings,bind,full-book,compile,epub,ebook,glossary,pipeline} ... Stage 0 `convert` turns an EPUB, a text-based PDF or a TXT into Markdown (docling, no OCR for image-based PDFs), then four LangGraph agents, a dictionary funnel, a glossary pass, a reversible chunker, a per-chunk glossary matcher, a front/back matter localizer, a chunk translator, a heading postprocessor and a binder turn that Markdown book into a consistent translation: `split` cuts it into chapters without reading the body, `preprocess` repairs each chapter's headers and conversion damage one chapter at a time, `dictionary` reduces each chapter to the sentences that carry a named entity, `glossary` locks one rendering per term, `chunk` cuts each chapter into sentence-safe chunks that concatenate back exactly, `chunk- glossary` tags every chunk and attaches the glossary terms it mentions, `matter` localizes the front/back matter before translation (no dictionary, web-searched title, BleBel credit, original-edition material omitted), `translate` translates the body chunks in reading order with those terms, keeping each call's whole prompt for debugging, `concatenate` glues the translated chunks back into one file per chapter, `postprocess` makes the translated chapter titles, other headings and table of contents consistent without reading the prose, `openings` audits (and repairs) every chapter's first lines with no model at all, and `bind` concatenates the postprocessed chapters into one Markdown book. Sources come from data/input/, output goes to data/output/<book>/. positional arguments: {convert,tools,inspect,split,scan,preprocess,dictionary,chunk,chunk-glossary,matter,translate,concatenate,assemble,postprocess,openings,bind,full-book,compile,epub,ebook,glossary,pipeline} convert stage 0: convert an EPUB, a text-based PDF or a TXT to Markdown (docling; image-based PDFs are rejected instead of OCR'd) tools list the tools, grouped by pipeline stage inspect deterministic structural report (no LLM; runs stage 0 for a non-Markdown source) split stage 1: run the agent and write chapter files scan stage 2 pre-flight: header evidence and damage profile (no LLM, no writes) preprocess stage 2: clean each chapter, one chapter at a time, and write the result dictionary stage 3: reduce each chapter to its entity-bearing sentences (sentence split -> uppercase filter -> 4-word floor -> NER gate), then to the sentences that introduce a noun (first mentions only) chunk stage 5: cut each chapter into translation-sized chunks without breaking paragraphs or sentences; every chunk is an exact source slice and the manifest records its chapter and global order chunk-glossary stage 6: run NER over every chunk first, then fuzzy- match each extracted term against glossary.json (rapidfuzz) and write the relevant terms per chunk, under the chunk's own name matter stage 6b: localize the front/back matter before translation with its own LangGraph agent — no dictionary, a web-searched published title, the BleBel credit, original-edition material omitted, published formatting translate stage 7: translate every chunk in reading order, with the glossary rows it mentions, into 07-translations/ (English -> Serbian by default) and keep the whole prompt of each call in 07-translation-prompts/ concatenate (assemble) stage 8: concatenate the translated chunks back into one file per chapter, in a separate 08-translated- chapters/ folder postprocess stage 9: postprocess the translated chapters' headings and table of contents in a separate folder, without reading chapter prose openings final phase of stages 2 and 9: audit every chapter's first lines and remove the safe leftovers (no LLM) bind (full-book, compile) stage 10: concatenate the postprocessed chapters into one Markdown book epub (ebook) stage 11: package the postprocessed chapters as an EPUB 3 book (images embedded, reader navigation instead of the printed TOC) glossary stage 4: walk the reduced chapters first to last and build one book-wide dictionary (term, category, locked target-language translation, context) with an LLM, feeding each chapter the dictionary so far pipeline run the whole pipeline (same driver as scripts/run_pipeline.py) options: -h, --help show this help message and exit
